paragraphs: This paper examines a vulnerability in language models that accept audio: sound can interfere with safety behavior even when its spoken content is benign. The authors focus on Acoustic Latent Semantics, meaning underlying paralinguistic features associated with the priors of audio generation models. Their central finding is that these features can compromise safety alignment without embedding a harmful instruction in the audio itself.

The proposed Acoustic Interference Attack separates the malicious text request from the accompanying sound. It uses reusable, instruction-neutral interference audio rather than optimizing a new audio payload for each request. This distinction matters because it changes the role of audio from carrying an instruction to influencing how the model processes instructions supplied through another modality.

Experiments covering 10 audio language models and five datasets report state-of-the-art attack success. An interpretability analysis also identifies changes in the models’ inference paths and effective patterns within the acoustic features. Together, these results identify cross-modal alignment as a security concern: harmless audio content does not necessarily imply harmless effects on the processing of accompanying text.
icml-2026-acoustic-interference-a-new-pa.tldr: Reusable audio with benign content can interfere with audio language models’ safety alignment and enable jailbreaks through accompanying text.

paragraphs: Serving language models becomes more complicated when requests invoke external services during generation. Requests can move through different execution states, so a batch no longer consists of uniformly progressing text generation jobs. The paper argues that systems which ignore these changes and allocate a fixed token budget per batch can suffer severe head-of-line blocking, where queued work is delayed behind other requests.

AugServe addresses this problem through two coordinated scheduling decisions. It schedules requests using their current execution states and adjusts the token budget assigned to each batch. These mechanisms allow the serving system to respond to differences between requests and to changes that occur while a request is running. The objective is to reduce queuing delays while increasing effective throughput under strict service requirements.

The reported experiments show effective throughput improvements of 6.5 times over vLLM and 4.7 times over INFERCEPT. These are results for the evaluated workloads involving external calls. The contribution is a serving design that treats those calls and their changing execution states as scheduling information, connecting request management directly to the behavior of augmented language models.
icml-2026-augserve-adaptive-request-sche.tldr: AugServe adapts request scheduling and batch token budgets to external-call execution states, substantially improving measured effective throughput.

paragraphs: Generative image super-resolution can produce convincing detail that does not faithfully reflect the underlying image. This paper attributes that problem to a mismatch between training objectives that treat directions uniformly and the frequency structure of natural images. In particular, it argues that spectrally flat Gaussian noise in preference optimization does not adequately distinguish genuine fine detail from hallucinated detail.

The proposed ASASR framework changes the geometry of the generative process using a Sobolev construction. Its noise transition is explicitly colored so that its frequency profile follows natural spectral decay. This makes frequency structure part of the optimization itself. A learned adversary then constructs targeted negative examples corresponding to worst-case Sobolev gradients, directing training toward plausible ways that image structure can fail.

Evaluations report improvements over leading generative baselines, especially in spectral consistency and structural fidelity, together with reduced artifacts. The significance is the connection between how training noise is shaped and what restoration errors the model learns to distinguish. The approach aims to make generated detail more faithful by combining frequency-aware geometry with deliberately challenging structural examples.
icml-2026-coloring-the-noise-adversarial.tldr: ASASR reshapes training noise and constructs adversarial structural errors to improve the fidelity of generative image super-resolution.

paragraphs: DLM-Scope adapts sparse autoencoders to interpreting diffusion language models. These tools extract a relatively small collection of interpretable features from model activations, giving researchers a way to inspect internal representations and intervene on behavior. The paper demonstrates that trained Top-K sparse autoencoders can faithfully extract such features from diffusion models, extending a technique already widely used with autoregressive language models.

A notable finding is that inserting these autoencoders has different effects across the two model families. In autoregressive models, insertion typically increases loss. In the studied diffusion models, insertion into early layers can instead reduce cross-entropy loss, with this effect absent or much weaker in autoregressive models. Feature-based interventions during diffusion also often outperform steering in autoregressive models.

The authors further find that the extracted features provide useful signals for deciding decoding order and remain stable during diffusion-model post-training. These observations give the framework a role beyond explaining individual behaviors: its features may also inform generation algorithms. The results establish useful interpretability capabilities while showing that conclusions drawn from autoregressive models do not automatically describe diffusion models.
icml-2026-dlm-scope-mechanistic-interpre.tldr: DLM-Scope extracts interpretable diffusion-language-model features that support steering, decoding analysis, and sometimes lower early-layer loss.

paragraphs: Anchor-based clustering uses representative anchors to make grouping large datasets more efficient. When data have multiple views, the anchors must also capture useful distinctions within each view. The paper identifies a weakness in methods that learn anchors and assign clusters relatively separately: information about the eventual groups does not sufficiently shape the anchors, allowing redundant coverage and unclear cluster boundaries.

DCMC connects these processes through alignment in both directions between anchor representations and clustering representations. It begins with anchors specific to each view, then jointly improves sample-to-anchor assignments and cluster assignments. Alternating optimization allows the developing clusters to calibrate the anchors while the anchors continue to guide clustering. The design promotes semantic agreement across views while retaining the distinctions that make individual views useful.

The experiments report better performance than state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks. The contribution is therefore more than an alternative anchor initialization strategy. It makes anchor quality depend on the grouping structure being learned, addressing the separation between representation selection and cluster assignment that motivates the work.
icml-2026-dual-calibration-multi-view-cl.tldr: DCMC jointly calibrates anchors and cluster assignments to improve multi-view clustering while preserving useful differences between views.

paragraphs: Removing reflections from a single image is difficult because reflected content and the scene behind it can be visually ambiguous. EvReflection adds dynamic evidence from an event camera. The paper uses small differences in motion between the reflection and transmission layers to help distinguish them, providing information that a static RGB frame alone does not supply.

The network first uses a Micro-Dynamics Decoupler to separate motion cues associated with the two layers in the event stream. These cues then guide a Parallax-Attention Rectifier that removes reflection artifacts from the RGB image. To support training and evaluation, the authors also develop a simulation pipeline that accounts for parallax and introduce EVR², which they describe as the first real-world dataset for this task.

Experiments report state-of-the-art results on synthetic and real-world benchmarks. Relative to the best competing method, the reported PSNR improvements exceed 1.6 dB and 1.2 dB, respectively. The findings support using differences in layer motion as practical evidence for reflection separation, connecting an additional sensing modality to the ambiguity responsible for residual artifacts.
icml-2026-evreflection-event-driven-micr.tldr: EvReflection uses event-camera motion cues to separate reflections from underlying scenes and improve image restoration.

paragraphs: Autoformalization translates mathematical statements into formal representations, making preservation of meaning central to its usefulness. A binary judgment or single score can indicate that a translation failed without explaining the failure. FormalRx addresses that diagnostic gap by organizing evaluation around what went wrong, where it happened, and how the translation could be corrected.

Its SCI Error Taxonomy divides errors into 28 hierarchical categories with a strict priority ordering. The framework uses this structure to provide four outputs: an alignment judgment, an error category, an error location, and a correction. The authors implement these capabilities in FormalRx-8B, trained on 56,287 synthetic examples with detailed diagnostic annotations, and introduce FormalRx-Test as a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark.

FormalRx-8B reports F1 scores of 0.88 for alignment judgments and 0.71 for categorization, plus accuracies of 0.75 for localization and 0.73 for correction. It substantially outperforms the evaluated general-purpose and specialized baselines. These results support evaluating translation quality through actionable diagnosis, giving both human reviewers and automated improvement systems more specific information than an overall correctness score.
icml-2026-formalrx-rectify-and-examine-s.tldr: FormalRx diagnoses mathematical autoformalization failures by classifying, locating, and correcting semantic errors.

paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented generation often searches an index that remains unchanged after construction. Consequently, related questions can repeatedly require similar multi-step searches. GAM-RAG introduces a training-free retrieval memory that accumulates experience from successful queries, making evidence useful for similar reasoning patterns easier to activate during later retrieval.

The framework builds a lightweight hierarchical index whose links represent potential co-occurrence rather than fixed semantic relationships. Successful retrieval episodes supply feedback at the sentence level. An uncertainty-aware update rule, inspired by Kalman filtering, adjusts both sentence memories and estimates of their uncertainty. Reliable new information receives faster updates, while established memories or noisy feedback receive more conservative changes. This connects adaptation speed to the reliability and novelty of the evidence.

The paper provides theoretical analysis of these updates and reports an average performance improvement of 3.95% over the strongest baseline, rising to 8.19% with five-turn memory, alongside a 61% reduction in inference cost. The findings suggest that retrieval experience can improve both effectiveness and efficiency without training the language model, by changing which evidence becomes accessible over repeated interactions.
icml-2026-gam-rag-gain-adaptive-memory-f.tldr: GAM-RAG learns from retrieval episodes through uncertainty-aware memory updates, improving reported performance while reducing inference cost.

paragraphs: GeoEvo studies federated learning when clients have different combinations of data modalities. It treats each combination as a structural identity that places the client on its own curved mathematical space. The objective is a collaborative equilibrium compatible with those identities, allowing personalization without requiring every client to approach a single full-modality solution.

The authors formulate this objective as an identity-aware potential game. Their approximate solver combines curvature-adaptive Fisher descent with evolutionary search lifted between manifolds. Natural Evolution Strategies help escape optimization basins, while Particle Swarm updates use a server-broadcast Fréchet prototype to support transfer across clients. Together, these components connect local geometric optimization with broader search and shared information.

A monotone selection rule guarantees descent of a surrogate objective and a stationarity rate of order one over the square root of the iteration count. Further conclusions depend on lift residuals: controlled residuals imply expected potential dissipation, and vanishing residuals support convergence toward first-order Nash equilibria. Experiments report improved personalization and robustness across varied missing-modality patterns, complementing these explicitly conditional theoretical results.
icml-2026-geoevo-identity-aware-potentia.tldr: GeoEvo uses geometric optimization and evolutionary search to support personalized federated collaboration across clients with different available modalities.

paragraphs: Large reasoning models can spend excessive effort checking their own answers or exploring additional directions. This paper connects such overthinking and overshoot to expressions of doubt, particularly transitional conjunctions that introduce further reasoning. The authors argue that these moments can extend redundant checking or misdirected exploration when the model receives no timely feedback about its current progress.

Conjunction-Guided Intervention pauses reasoning at these markers so an external evaluator can assess the current state. A human or another language model evaluates rationality and completeness, providing feedback that helps determine whether reasoning should continue or terminate. The target model is trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization to adapt to this interactive process. Intervention timing therefore follows observable features of the reasoning rather than a fixed schedule.

Experiments report a better balance between accuracy and reasoning length. The approach matters because it connects computation control to specific moments when the model appears inclined to extend its reasoning. External feedback can then distinguish useful continuation from unnecessary elaboration, allowing the system to reduce redundancy while seeking to preserve answer accuracy.
icml-2026-intervene-when-it-doubts-conju.tldr: CGI pauses reasoning at linguistic signs of doubt and uses external feedback to reduce unnecessary reasoning while preserving accuracy.

paragraphs: Combining stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics with Gibbs updates offers a scalable way to approximate Bayesian inference in models with latent variables. The practical difficulty is choosing hyperparameters so that the resulting uncertainty estimates remain statistically meaningful. This paper develops a scaling-limit theory to explain how the algorithm’s different sources of randomness interact and to turn that explanation into tuning guidance.

Under appropriate rescaling of space and time, the authors derive a joint limiting process for global parameters and individual latent variables. Global parameters approach a diffusion-type process, while latent variables approach a jump process because their Gibbs updates occur intermittently. Analyzing these components together reveals how latent-variable randomness influences the stationary distribution of the global parameters.

The theory supplies explicit hyperparameter guidance for meaningful uncertainty quantification. In the reported experiments, SGLD-Gibbs tuned using this guidance produces better parameter estimates and uncertainty quantification than stochastic variational inference. The contribution connects scalable computation with statistical interpretation: it explains why tuning must account for latent updates as well as the evolution of global parameters.
icml-2026-large-scale-uncertainty-quanti.tldr: A joint jump-diffusion theory provides principled tuning guidance for scalable Bayesian uncertainty estimation with SGLD-Gibbs.

paragraphs: This paper asks how to estimate U-statistics efficiently when obtaining the necessary labels is expensive. Its framework actively selects informative labels within a fixed budget while preserving valid statistical inference. The aim is to extract more estimation value from each queried label without losing the reliability of the resulting uncertainty statements.

The central estimator is an augmented inverse probability weighting U-statistic. It incorporates both the rule used to select labels and predictions supplied by a machine learning model. This explicitly connects estimation to the selective sampling process. The authors characterize the sampling rule that minimizes variance and develop practical strategies based on that characterization, turning the statistical objective into guidance for deciding which labels to acquire.

The framework also extends to empirical risk minimization based on U-statistics, connecting label acquisition with learning objectives. Experiments on real datasets show substantial improvements in estimation efficiency over baseline methods while maintaining target coverage. The findings support a combination of selective labeling, predictive models, and sampling-aware estimation as a way to use limited annotation resources more effectively.
icml-2026-learning-u-statistics-with-act.tldr: An active-labeling framework improves U-statistic estimation efficiency under a fixed budget while preserving valid statistical inference.

paragraphs: Small language models are appealing for inexpensive agents, but long interactions can exceed their ability to retain decision-relevant state. Summarizing history in unstructured prose can also omit critical facts or gradually distort the state. LightWM addresses this problem for procedure-centric task families whose workflows recur, organizing memory around the structure of the work.

The framework decomposes a task into subgoals and maintains two memory levels: global memory for the overall task and local memory for the current subtask. Local memory directly guides action selection and receives structured updates from new observations. A one-time offline pipeline uses a larger language model and a few successful traces to induce reusable schemas for each task family. Deployment requires neither small-model parameter updates nor online calls to the larger model.

On ALFWorld valid_unseen, Qwen3-4B with LightWM reaches a success rate of 0.910, while representative prompting and earlier working-memory baselines remain below 0.320 under the same setting. This result supports structured, reusable memory as an effective way to improve extended procedural execution in the evaluated small-model agent.
icml-2026-lightwm-training-free-hierarch.tldr: LightWM equips small-model agents with reusable structured memories, substantially improving success on the reported ALFWorld evaluation without online large-model calls.

paragraphs: Long-term forecasting requires models to preserve repeating patterns, distinguish trends from rapid fluctuations, and track relationships between variables. This paper argues that increasing network depth can weaken periodic information and entangle trend and noise. It also identifies a tradeoff in treating channels independently: training may become more stable, but coordination among variables can be disrupted.

PESD-TSF addresses these issues through three connected designs. Multiplicative Periodic Gating uses continuous-time priors to modulate amplitudes and retain periodic structure across layers. A multi-scale encoder combines detrended attention with hierarchical sampling to separate longer-term trends from high-frequency variation. Cross-Scale Collaborative Attention and RLC regularization then reconstruct relationships among variables in deep representations, using orthogonality and consistency constraints to encourage physically consistent coordination.

Experiments across multiple domains report consistently state-of-the-art forecasting performance, with particularly strong gains when variables have complex coupling. The results support the framework’s emphasis on explicitly preserving different kinds of temporal structure. Its contribution combines periodic modeling, structured decomposition, and inter-variable collaboration within one forecasting architecture, rather than leaving these relationships implicit in deeper representations.
icml-2026-pesd-tsf-a-period-aware-and-ex.tldr: PESD-TSF improves long-term forecasting by explicitly preserving periodicity, separating temporal components, and modeling coordination between variables.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary segmentation assigns semantic labels to individual pixels using arbitrary text queries. Image-text models can generalize to unfamiliar categories, but image-level training does not necessarily support precise boundaries or coherent regions. The paper also argues that real-valued alignment mixes magnitude and phase information, limiting the quality of fine-grained correspondence between language and image features.

PhaseAlign represents visual and textual embeddings in a complex domain and explicitly separates their magnitude and phase. Inspired by phase-controlled interference in electromagnetic waves, this design seeks more stable alignment between the modalities. The framework also models local neighborhoods through multi-scale spatial contrast normalization. A further component uses self-attention from a pretrained vision transformer to propagate category activations and improve spatial coherence.

Experiments report state-of-the-art performance across multiple open-vocabulary segmentation benchmarks. The design links two sources of improvement: refining the representation used for image-text matching and strengthening the spatial relationships used to turn those matches into pixel labels. The stated gains in boundary clarity and region integrity address the blurred and fragmented outputs that motivate the approach.
icml-2026-phasealign-complex-phase-align.tldr: PhaseAlign separates embedding magnitude and phase while modeling spatial relationships to improve open-vocabulary segmentation.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation constructs a compact surrogate dataset that retains useful training information. Generative approaches can make this process faster, but the paper identifies two difficulties with diffusion-based methods: sequential denoising complicates direct matching to representative prototypes, and generation can become disconnected from the target task. As a result, synthetic samples may drift away from the desired distribution.

ProtoVAR uses visual autoregressive generation that predicts progressively finer scales. It injects class prototypes at multiple scales, giving generation explicit constraints on what representative class content should look like while preserving sample diversity. The coarse-to-fine structure supports semantic consistency throughout generation. A pool-based selector then chooses a compact, task-aligned dataset from the resulting candidates.

Experiments report state-of-the-art performance with computational cost comparable to or lower than diffusion-based distillation. The contribution connects guidance during generation with selection afterward: prototypes shape the candidate images, and the selector determines which candidates form the final surrogate dataset. The findings support using task-relevant representative structure throughout the distillation process instead of relying on generation quality alone.
icml-2026-protovar-efficient-dataset-dis.tldr: ProtoVAR combines multi-scale prototype-guided image generation with selection to produce effective compact training datasets at competitive computational cost.

paragraphs: Single-cell RNA sequencing profiles are sparse, high-dimensional, and unordered. Generating them autoregressively imposes an artificial sequence and can accumulate errors across generation steps. scDiVa instead uses masked discrete diffusion, with a continuous-time process that masks tokens in a way intended to align with dropout-like corruption in the data.

A bidirectional denoiser jointly models which genes are present and their continuous expression values. Entropy-normalized serialization supports information efficiency, while a latent anchor token preserves the cell’s global identity. Training combines depth-invariant time sampling with a dual denoising objective, exposing the model to different sparsity levels and teaching it to recover both gene identity and expression magnitude. These components link the corruption process to the two kinds of information that need reconstruction.

After pretraining on 59 million cells, scDiVa shows strong transfer performance on benchmarks for batch integration, cell type annotation, and perturbation response prediction. The results suggest that masked discrete diffusion is an effective and biologically coherent alternative to autoregression for these data. They connect the model’s representation and generation choices to the unordered, sparse structure of cellular profiles.
icml-2026-scdiva-masked-discrete-diffusi.tldr: scDiVa jointly reconstructs gene identities and expression values through masked diffusion, showing strong transfer across single-cell analysis tasks.

paragraphs: Medical audio models trained on small, imbalanced datasets can become overconfident when predictions depend too heavily on feature magnitude. This paper calls that problem norm bias. It considers Equiangular Tight Frames, geometric arrangements with strong angular class separation, but argues that existing implementations struggle with noisy medical data because rotations are unstable and class prototypes move during training.

Spherical Procrustes Alignment combines two branches to address these problems. A spherical branch normalizes features to remove norm bias. A geometric branch adapts features and dynamically aligns a fixed Equiangular Tight Frame with changing prototypes through Procrustes alignment. A self-alignment mechanism fuses the branches to optimize prediction scores jointly, bringing normalized semantic alignment together with adaptive class geometry.

Experiments on ICBHI 2017 and CirCor DigiScope report state-of-the-art performance without additional inference cost. The stated findings connect prediction accuracy with more reliable uncertainty behavior in the evaluated medical audio tasks. The approach matters because its geometric adaptation addresses both unequal feature magnitudes and prototype drift, two mechanisms the paper identifies as obstacles to dependable predictions.
icml-2026-spherical-procrustes-alignment.tldr: SPA combines normalized features with dynamically aligned class geometry to improve medical audio prediction and reliability without extra inference cost.

paragraphs: Language-model distillation can train a student using sampled teacher tokens, called hard labels, or the teacher’s full next-token probabilities, called soft labels. Although soft labels contain richer information, this paper finds that combining the two consistently works better. The authors attribute the benefit to reduced exposure bias, the mismatch between training and inference distributions, rather than closer teacher matching during training.

Their Bridge–Garden theory divides generation steps into those requiring an exact next token and those allowing flexibility. Hard-label training performs well at the exact steps by avoiding risky deviations, while soft-label training preserves diversity where multiple continuations are acceptable. A hybrid can address both demands across a sequence. The authors use this account to develop supervision methods that adaptively balance hard and soft labels.

Across seven teacher–student pairs and reasoning and coding benchmarks, the proposed methods outperform divergence-based and on-policy distillation baselines while reporting a 9.7-fold reduction in training cost. The findings explain why copying a richer teacher distribution is not by itself the whole objective: student behavior during its own generation also depends on where precision and flexibility are needed.
icml-2026-the-bridge-garden-dilemma-in-l.tldr: Mixing hard and soft distillation labels helps students balance exact and flexible generation steps, reducing exposure bias.

paragraphs: As an autoregressive model generates text, it produces a sequence of hidden states. This paper asks how to compress that sequence into a useful representation of the model’s internal state. The key choice is whether one generated token provides a sufficient summary or whether information spread across several tokens should be combined.

The authors study representations derived from generated tokens and compare them with grounded embeddings across several domains. They find that pooling token embeddings produces more informative representations than using any individual token. This observation is consistent with semantic information being distributed throughout generation. It therefore supports aggregation across positions rather than assuming that a particular token contains the most useful overall representation.

The study also uses alignment to examine how internal representations evolve as generation proceeds. In this setting, pooling provides a more reliable summary of that evolving state. The result concerns how to read and summarize generated representations: a sequence can carry useful semantic information collectively even when no single position captures it as well. The evidence supports distributed information without establishing that every token contributes equally.
icml-2026-the-truth-lies-somewhere-in-th.tldr: Pooling representations across generated tokens provides a more informative summary of model state than selecting any individual token.

paragraphs: Detecting AI-generated images can benefit from combining semantic information with texture-level artifacts. This paper identifies a problem in that combination: artifact features can be highly similar to one another, producing nearly uniform attention after softmax. Such attention dilution makes it harder for a multimodal language model to fuse artifact evidence effectively with semantic evidence.

TranX-Adapter introduces a lightweight, two-direction fusion mechanism. Task-aware Optimal-Transport Fusion transfers artifact information into semantic features, using Jensen–Shannon divergence between their prediction probabilities to construct the transport cost. X-Fusion transfers semantic information in the other direction through cross-attention. The two pathways therefore use different mechanisms to exchange information, addressing the specific attention problem identified for artifact features.

Experiments on standard detection benchmarks with several advanced multimodal language models show consistent, significant improvements, reaching up to 6% in accuracy. The findings support improving how the two feature types interact, beyond simply providing both to the model. The task-aware transport component connects fusion to prediction behavior, while the reverse pathway brings semantic context into the artifact representation.
icml-2026-tranx-adapter-bridging-artifac.tldr: TranX-Adapter improves AI-generated image detection by exchanging artifact and semantic information through transport-based fusion and cross-attention.

paragraphs: Scientific machine learning models can behave qualitatively differently under different hyperparameter settings. This paper studies those differences as training regimes: configurations within a regime show consistent behavior, while configurations across regimes can fail in distinct ways. Its diagnostic framework examines performance, training dynamics, and loss-landscape geometry together to identify these patterns.

The authors report a recurring three-regime structure across many standard scientific machine learning models, constraint-enforcement choices, and optimizer designs. They also find that optimization effectiveness depends on the regime, with no single method working well across all studied regimes. More detailed failure modes can challenge conventional interpretations of standard loss-landscape metrics, showing why those measurements need to be considered alongside actual training behavior and performance.

The findings are validated with physics-informed neural networks, neural operators, and neural ordinary differential equations on representative differential-equation benchmarks. The contribution is a diagnostic perspective that can organize failures across tasks and model families. Its practical implication is that guidance for improving robustness should account for the current training regime, because an optimization choice that helps one regime may not work well in another.
icml-2026-unveiling-multi-regime-pattern.tldr: A joint analysis of training behavior and geometry reveals three recurring SciML regimes with different failure modes and optimization needs.

paragraphs: A multi-agent system can execute its actions correctly and still fail because it misjudged whether its knowledge supported the plan. The paper calls this epistemic miscalibration in planning. Such errors can remain hidden inside plans that are self-consistent and executable. Changing information also makes them difficult to track, because later assessments can obscure the discrepancies that exposed earlier mistakes.

EPC-AW evaluates whether plans remain supported under different information conditions. Its plan-selection component favors plans whose evaluations are stable across agents. A second component refines epistemic state over time, using past discrepancies to guide later planning. The workflow thus combines consistency-based selection with a mechanism for retaining and using evidence of previous miscalibration.

Experiments report an average 9.75% improvement in system-level success. The mechanism assesses the stability of support for a plan rather than directly verifying feasibility, an important distinction in what its checks establish. The results suggest that improving how agents assess and update their knowledge can improve outcomes even when the underlying problem is not incorrect action execution.
icml-2026-when-planning-fails-despite-co.tldr: EPC-AW improves multi-agent planning by checking support across information conditions and using past discrepancies to refine later judgments.

paragraphs: This paper asks what role medical specialist models should retain as general-purpose language models become more capable in healthcare. Its proposed answer is collaboration among generalist models, domain-specific models, and clinicians. The authors argue that broad reasoning ability and specialized analysis offer complementary strengths that a medical AI system should coordinate.

HetMedAgent implements that idea through a heterogeneous multi-agent framework. It combines evidence while accounting for conflicts, uses uncertainty to trigger clinician intervention, and adaptively calibrates thresholds. These mechanisms address how the participating models’ outputs are reconciled and when human expertise enters the process. The framework therefore makes coordination and disagreement handling central to the system’s design.

Experiments on three real-world clinical decision-making tasks show that the combined system significantly outperforms either model type used alone. The authors interpret this as evidence for the continuing value of specialists in modality-specific analysis. The stated findings support the collaborative architecture in the evaluated tasks, showing that general reasoning and domain-specific precision can contribute jointly. They also make clinician participation part of the proposed workflow rather than treating model collaboration as a replacement for expertise.
icml-2026-why-specialist-models-still-ma.tldr: HetMedAgent combines generalist models, medical specialists, and clinician intervention, outperforming either model type alone on three clinical tasks.

paragraphs: GRPO trains reasoning models using verifiable rewards, but estimating how useful an individual thought is can be noisy without a value model. This paper investigates why sampling several continuations from the same thought can reduce that noise. Its analysis distinguishes the number of sampled thoughts from the number of continuations sampled for each thought.

Using the multivariate delta method in a minimal tree-style setting, the authors find an asymmetry. Increasing the number of thoughts leaves a strictly positive estimation-variance floor. Increasing continuations per thought instead drives the leading-order variance toward zero at a rate inversely proportional to that continuation count. Within the studied fixed-temperature, value-model-free estimator, sampling more thoughts alone therefore cannot deliver accurate thought-level advantage estimates.

Experiments provide further evidence for improved optimization stability, training efficiency, and final performance across mathematics, vision, and different model architectures and sizes. The theoretical conclusion is scoped to the estimator analyzed, and the paper describes branching as potentially necessary. Its contribution explains why allocating samples to repeated continuations can matter in a way that simply broadening the set of sampled thoughts does not.
icml-2026-why-tree-style-branching-matte.tldr: For the studied GRPO estimator, sampling more continuations per thought reduces variance in a way that sampling more thoughts alone cannot.
